faqs.q: What are the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers used for?
faqs.a: Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers pull bearings, gears and pulleys off shafts with a hydraulic cylinder, in 2-jaw and 3-jaw versions. The listing has 16 models from 10 to 64 ton, such as the LGH-210 and LGH-324. This listing carries 16 part numbers.

faqs.q: Which sizes are the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers available in?
faqs.a: The listing carries 16 part numbers in 10, 14, 24, 53 and 64 ton, such as LGH210, LGHNC214, LGHNC310, LGH324 and LGH253, in 2 jaw and 3 jaw versions with a hydraulic cylinder.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right size or model of the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers?
faqs.a: Choose the capacity from 10 to 64 ton and the number of jaws, 2 or 3, for the part to be pulled, then check the reach and spread against the shaft and the work. Pullers in this listing need a separate pump.

faqs.q: What pressure rating do the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers have?
faqs.a: The maker states a pulling capacity in tons for each model of the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers, and the size table gives it for every part number. The capacity is the force the puller develops at its rated hydraulic pressure, so use a pump that matches the tool and never exceed the stated capacity.

faqs.q: Which materials are the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers offered in?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the materials of the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers. Pullers are loaded in tension through their legs and jaws, so ask us for the maker's data on the alloy and heat treatment if the job is heavy or critical.

faqs.q: Which standards and documents apply to the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers?
faqs.a: The listing names no ISO, ASME or EN standard for the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers and holds no certificates. If your site requires a test certificate or a conformity document, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue.

faqs.q: What do the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers connect to?
faqs.a: The Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers grip the part to be pulled with its jaws and pulls against the shaft or the housing, so the reach and spread must fit the job. Hydraulic sets include the pump, and master sets add attachments for bearings and gears.

faqs.q: How should the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Before using the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers, check the jaws and legs for wear and cracks, centre the puller on the shaft and pull square, and keep the pull inside the stated capacity. Stand clear of the line of pull, because a part or a jaw that lets go can be thrown.

faqs.q: Where are the Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers used?
faqs.a: The Enerpac LGH hydraulic lock grip pullers are used to pull bearings, gears, pulleys, couplings and sleeves off shafts in maintenance shops, power plants, steel mills and mines, where a hydraulic pull is needed instead of heating and hammering.

faqs.a: The LGH pullers are the puller alone with a hydraulic cylinder in 16 part numbers of 10 to 64 ton, while [the Enerpac LGHS hydraulic lock grip puller sets](/p/enerpac-lghs-hydraulic-lock-grip-puller-sets) are sets that add a pump, in 24 part numbers.
